newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama to create commission to negotiate U.S. bases.
newsitem.headline: Panama to create commission to negotiate U.S. bases.

text.p: The Panamanian government plans to create a commission to negotiate the future of U.S. military bases in the country, Foreign Minister Ricardo Alberto Arias said on Wednesday.
Arias said President Ernesto Perez Balladares would name the commission, which would resume talks that broke down almost a year ago.
Under the 1977 Panama Canal treaties the United States has begun to transfer control of the canal and surrounding military installations to Panama.

Fort Amador, a Second World War U.S. nerve centre, was officially handed over this month, seven other bases are due to be handed over by Dec. 31, 1999, and 7,500 troops will pull out. Exploratory talks about maintaining a U.S. military presence in Panama were due to begin last year but broke down when Washington refused to pay for the bases.
Arias added that John Negropote, the U.S. coordinator of the Panama bases talks, would visit Panama shortly to review plans to turn Howard Air Force Base into an international drug fighting centre.
